name: International Protection (UNHCR Mandate RSD)

requirements.blocker_text: Must establish a well-founded fear of persecution to UNHCR, which processes asylum claims directly for Grenada (no dedicated domestic asylum legislation or national refugee status determination procedure).

evidence_required.document: Personal account/testimony at UNHCR RSD interview

sources.title: UNHCR Northern and Eastern Caribbean -- Apply for Asylum through UNHCR: confirms Grenada is among the countries/territories (alongside Anguilla, Antigua and Barbuda, Barbados, Bermuda, British Virgin Islands, Dominica, Haiti, Saint Kitts and Nevis, Saint Lucia, Saint Vincent and the Grenadines, Sint Maarten) where UNHCR processes asylum claims directly rather than the local government

notes: NEW ROUTE, part of Grenada's initial build. Built as draft (not excluded) following this session's established three-bucket humanitarian framework: a real process exists (UNHCR direct-mandate RSD, per the same regional page used for the other UNHCR-direct-processing-group countries built this session), and no country-specific negative finding was located for Grenada specifically to justify exclusion instead. STATUS: DRAFT because sourcing is tier-2 (UNHCR regional page) only, with no Grenada-specific government source or detailed rights framework found -- modelled with the same conservative generic outcome (no work/study rights, family reunification only) used elsewhere. Note also that Grenada's own Citizenship Act contains a 'political refugees' and 'stateless persons' expedited naturalisation provision (Section 7(3) special-circumstances regulations -- see gd_naturalisation.json's notes) that is thinly documented but may be relevant to a recognized refugee's eventual path to citizenship, distinct from this initial protection-status route.
